messages:
From: Sam Jones <sam.jones@acmecloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: perf SLOs & concurrency (Acme)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick sync today — really helpful to talk through expected traffic patterns. Quick written recap so we're aligned and to capture a couple open questions: 

High-level targets:
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn generation (responses up to ~512 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained ~50 QPS across our fleet; capability to burst to ~500 QPS for ~10s during peak events.
- Concurrency: typical connection pooling will present ~200 concurrent open connections to your API (each may send parallel requests).
- Streaming: required for multi-k turn responses; we need chunked responses to display progressive text in our UI.
- Typical response size: ~120 tokens average; some longer responses up to ~1k tokens (rare).

Open questions we flagged on the call:
1) How does Redwood enforce rate limits (per-API-key QPS, per-minute token caps, per-connection limits)?
2) Can we request a soft quota increase for the pilot (sustained 100 QPS / burst 500 QPS) and what is the timeline for approval?
3) Any recommended connection pooling/keep-alive guidance to avoid head-of-line blocking on your infrastructure?

I've attached a simple SLO spreadsheet with our traffic profile and sample payload sizes (Acme_SLOs.xlsx). Can you confirm next steps and what you need from our side to get a pilot quota in place?

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Jones
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Cloud
sam.jones@acmecloud.com

Attachment: Acme_SLOs.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-endpoint QPS, token distributions)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: perf SLOs & concurrency (Acme)

Hi Sam — really appreciate the clear recap and the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. Quick confirmation from our side and proposed next steps: 

Confirmed notes:
- We can aim to validate p95 <= 200ms for the 512-token profile on our verified model variants; we will run a short profiling pass during the pilot to confirm.
- Streaming is supported and we will enable chunked responses for the pilot.
- For concurrency, our hosted tier has conservative default per-key QPS to protect noisy neighbors; we can propose a pilot quota for you while we assess capacity.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood: Provide a pilot quota proposal (sustained 100 QPS, burst 500 QPS for 30s windows) + expected per-minute token cap.
2) Acme: Confirm the top priority (streaming vs concurrency) and send any procurement constraints.
3) Infra sync: Vivek (cc'd internally) will model capacity & recommend if Dedicated is required for your sustained throughput.
4) Security/compliance: Neha will pull any SOC/comms items you need during pilot.

If that works, I will put together a formal pilot/quota doc and a short SOW for internal approval — should have something to you within 48 business hours.

One quick note on connection pooling: our recommended pattern is to use keep-alive with a modest connection pool per host (start with 50 persistent connections per service instance) and prefer request-level parallelism rather than very long-lived multiplexed streams. We'll include a short guide in the pilot packet.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_pilot_checklist.pdf (pilot checklist and recommended pool settings)

Subject: Fwd: Follow-up: perf SLOs & concurrency (Acme) — quota ask

Forwarding Sam's email and our reply — Acme is asking for pilot/quota guidance. Key asks: streaming is a hard requirement, they expect ~200 concurrent connections, sustained 50 QPS with bursts to 500 QPS. They want a soft quota increase for the pilot (target: sustained 100 QPS / burst 500 QPS).

My proposal:
- Offer pilot quota: per-API-key sustained 100 QPS, burst up to 500 QPS for short windows (30s); token cap 2,000,000 tokens/minute for the key.
- Temporary per-connection limit: no more than 250 concurrent connections per API key; recommend they use ~50 persistent connections per instance and rely on request-level parallelism.
- If profiling indicates we can't meet p95=200ms on hosted for their 1k-token tails, recommend Dedicated pool (simple pricing attach).

Action items:
- Vivek: can you run a quick capacity model (guesstimate GPU slots needed) and confirm whether a hosted pilot at these quotas is safe for the next 30 days? Flag any risk.
- Neha: prepare a short note on whether any compliance gating is needed for pilot (SOC2 evidence, data handling).
- I'll draft the pilot/quota doc and attach our standard draft terms for temporary quota adjustments.
